subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow `read` fallback for known binary document formats now, or wait for broader document parsing/provider-native file architecture?
rationale: Current source still has the token-waste behavior, but the issue explicitly offers fallback versus parsing paths and related open issues cover wider document ingestion architecture.

options.title: Land a narrow fallback
options.body: Guard known PDF/Office document reads in the read-tool path and return an actionable message while preserving text and image behavior.

options.title: Fold into document architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as context for broader document extraction/provider-native file work and close or supersede the conflicting guard PR after that direction is chosen.

options.title: Reject core handling
options.body: Decide that document parsing/avoidance belongs entirely in plugins or user tools and close this only after documenting the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow fallback
recommendation.body: Guard known PDF/Office document reads in the read-tool path and return an actionable message while preserving text and image behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read-tool source history points here and the decision crosses agent runtime and safe-default behavior.
